title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:
Role Overview

The Accounts Payable Assistant is a core member of the finance team, responsible for ensuring the accurate, efficient, and timely processing of high-volume supplier invoices and employee expenses. Based in our Milton Keynes office, this permanent role focuses on maintaining a precise purchase ledger, resolving financial queries, and facilitating weekly payment runs while ensuring strict adherence to internal financial controls.

Key Responsibilities

Invoice Processing & Ledger Management
- Accurately log, match, batch, and code high volumes of purchase invoices against corresponding purchase orders (POs) and delivery notes.
- Ensure all invoices are authorized by the appropriate department heads prior to payment.
- Maintain a clean, up-to-date, and accurate purchase ledger.
- Identify and investigate discrepancies between POs, delivery receipts, and supplier invoices.

Payment Runs & Reconciliations
- Prepare and process weekly and mid-month payment runs (BACS, CHAPS, and international transfers) accurately and on time.
- Perform regular supplier statement reconciliations, actively chasing missing invoices or credit notes to ensure account balances align.
- Process and reconcile employee out-of-pocket expenses and corporate credit card statements in line with company policy.
- Assist with month-end and year-end closing procedures, ensuring all AP timelines are met.

Query Resolution & Supplier Relations
- Serve as the primary point of contact for external supplier inquiries via phone and email, resolving payment disputes and account holds professionally.
- Liaise internally with procurement and operational teams to resolve unapproved invoices and PO discrepancies.
- Set up new supplier accounts and maintain accurate vendor master data, ensuring bank details are verified to prevent fraud.

Experience & Knowledge
- Proven track record working within an Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger, or general Finance Administration role.
- Strong understanding of standard double-entry bookkeeping and basic accounting principles.
- Familiarity with major ERP or accounting software (e.g., SAP, Sage, Oracle, Xero, or MS Dynamics).
- Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Excel (VLOOKUPs, Pivot Tables, and basic formulas).

Skills & Attributes
- Attention to Detail: Exceptional numerical accuracy and a meticulous approach to data entry.
- Time Management: Ability to manage a fast-paced workload, prioritize effectively, and meet strict daily and monthly deadlines.
- Communication: Clear, professional written and verbal communication skills for handling internal stakeholders and external suppliers.
- Reliability: A strong sense of accountability and comfort working fully on-site in a structured 9-to-5 team environment.

Compensation & Benefits
- Salary: 30,000 - 32,000
- Pension: Company pension scheme with employer contributions
- Holiday: 25 days annual leave plus standard UK bank holidays

title: Credit Controller (Part Time Hours)
description:
Credit Controller Part Time

Location: Milton Keynes
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am 1.00pm (Some flexibility can be discussed)
Department: Finance
Reporting to: Financial Controller

£32,000p/a Pro-Rata 20 Hours per week

Role Purpose

The Credit Controller will be responsible for the day-to-day management of the sales ledger and credit control function, ensuring customer receipts are accurately recorded, outstanding debts are actively managed and customer accounts are maintained effectively.

The role will work closely with customers and colleagues across the business to resolve account queries, maintain appropriate credit terms and support strong cash collection.

As part of the wider Finance team, the role will also provide general finance support and cover where required.

Key Responsibilities

Credit Control & Debt Collection
- Proactively chase customers for payment of outstanding invoices by telephone and email.
- Manage the aged debtor ledger, prioritising overdue and higher-risk accounts.
- Support new customer credit checks and the setting or review of appropriate credit limits.
- Run and review the aged debtor report regularly, identifying overdue balances and required actions.
- Escalate significantly overdue accounts, payment concerns and potential bad debts to the Financial Controller.
- Build effective relationships with customers to encourage prompt payment whilst maintaining good commercial relationships.
- Work with colleagues across Sales, Customer Service and other areas of the business to resolve invoice and payment queries quickly.

Daily Banking & Cash Allocation
- Review customer receipts on a daily basis.
- Post daily customer receipts and banking transactions accurately to the accounting system.
- Allocate receipts against the appropriate customer invoices and accounts.
- Investigate unidentified, underpaid or overpaid receipts.
- Ensure customer accounts are kept accurate and up to date.

Customer Statements & Account Management
- Prepare and send customer statements, reminder letters on a regular basis.
- Respond to customer account and statement queries.
- Reconcile customer accounts where required and investigate outstanding differences.
- Ensure customer master data and credit control information is maintained accurately.

Wider Finance Support
- Provide cover and support across the Finance team during holidays, absence and busy periods.
- Assist with general finance administration and transactional finance activities where required.
- Support month-end reporting relating to debtors, cash receipts and the sales ledger.
- Work collaboratively with other members of Finance to ensure deadlines are achieved.
- Contribute to improvements in finance processes, controls and ways of working.

Skills & Experience

Essential

Previous experience in a Credit Control, Sales Ledger or Accounts Receivable role.

Confident chasing customers for overdue payments by both telephone and email.

Experience of allocating customer receipts and maintaining customer accounts.

Good understanding of aged debtors, payment terms and credit control processes.

Good Excel skills.

Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

Confident communicating with customers and colleagues at different levels of the business.

Able to organise and prioritise workload independently.

Desirable

Experience working within a manufacturing, engineering or distribution environment.

Experience using Sage 200 or a similar accounting/ERP system.

Experience carrying out customer credit checks and monitoring credit limits.

Experience supporting month-end finance processes.

Personal Approach

We are looking for someone who is:
- Proactive and comfortable taking ownership of the debtor ledger.
- Confident but professional when chasing outstanding debt.
- Organised and methodical.
- Commercially aware and able to balance debt collection with maintaining good customer relationships.
- Comfortable communicating issues rather than allowing overdue debts or queries to remain unresolved.
- Flexible and willing to support the wider Finance team when needed.

title: Finance Administrator
company: Pro Staff Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Loan Administration & Finance Administrator
Location: Olney
Salary: 27-32 K DOE
Hours: 9.00 - 5.30

Are you organised, accurate and comfortable working with financial information? Do you enjoy getting stuck into the detail, keeping things running smoothly and making sure everything is where it should be?
We're looking for a Loan Administration & Finance Administrator to join a busy finance team, taking responsibility for the administration of customer loan agreements from initial setup through to settlement and closure.

This is a varied role offering the opportunity to develop your knowledge of lending and financial services, work with specialist finance systems and potentially work towards an AAT qualification with support from the business.
What will you be doing?

You'll play an important part in keeping the loan administration process running efficiently, making sure customer agreements and financial records are accurate and up to date.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Setting up and processing new loan agreements, checking customer details, figures, repayment schedules and supporting documentation.
- Preparing and issuing customer agreements, statements, payment schedules and other financial correspondence.
- Maintaining accurate customer and agreement records throughout the loan lifecycle.
- Processing amendments, calculating settlement figures and responding to customer and internal queries.
- Managing the administration of agreements reaching the end of their term, including settlements and account closures.
- Checking payments, outstanding balances and charges to ensure everything is correct.
- Supporting the finance team with reporting, reconciliations and audit information.
- Identifying discrepancies, investigating issues and helping improve administrative processes.

What are we looking for?
We're interested in someone who has a good head for figures, takes pride in getting things right and enjoys working in a structured administrative role.
Ideally, you'll have:
- Previous administration experience, within lending, financial services, banking, asset finance or a similar environment.
- Good numerical skills and confidence handling financial information.
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to your work.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Good communication skills and the confidence to deal with queries professionally.
- Experience using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word.
- A responsible approach to handling confidential customer and financial information.

Experience with loan management systems, Sage or contract administration would be an advantage, but isn't essential.
What's on offer?
- A varied role within an established finance function.
- Training on specialist loan management systems and internal processes.
- Support and training towards an AAT qualification, should you wish to pursue one.
- The opportunity to build your experience and develop within finance and financial services.

title: Practice Bookkeeper - High Wycombe
description:
Practice Bookkeeper - High Wycombe

£35,000 - £40,000 High Wycombe

Are you currently working as a Bookkeeper within an accountancy practice and looking for a firm where you can take genuine ownership of your clients and your work?

I'm recruiting for a long-established, award-winning accountancy firm in High Wycombe that is looking to add an experienced Practice Bookkeeper to its Outsourced Accounting Services team.

This is a firm with an excellent local reputation, a loyal client base and very strong staff retention. It has also entered an exciting new phase of growth, with significant investment behind the business and ambitious plans to grow its presence and ultimately become a Top 100 UK accountancy firm.

For someone joining now, that offers a nice combination: the security and client base of an established practice, but with considerably more going on than simply maintaining the status quo.

What will you be doing?

You'll look after bookkeeping work across a portfolio of external clients, with plenty of direct client contact and the autonomy to manage your own jobs.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Bookkeeping for a portfolio of external clients
- Posting sales, purchases, bank transactions and journals
- Preparing and reconciling control accounts
- Producing information required for management accounts
- Maintaining and writing up client cashbooks
- Preparing analysis, summaries and basic working papers
- Reviewing bookkeeping completed by other members of the team
- Liaising directly with clients to answer queries and finalise work
- Working across cloud accounting platforms including Xero, Sage and QuickBooks
- Undertaking bookkeeping at client premises where required

Who are they looking for?

Practice experience is essential for this position.

You should currently be working, or have very recently worked, as a Bookkeeper within an accountancy practice, looking after bookkeeping for multiple external clients.

You'll need:
- Current or recent accountancy practice bookkeeping experience
- Experience managing work across a portfolio of external clients
- Strong client-facing experience
- Confidence dealing directly with business owners and finance contacts
- Good working knowledge of Xero, Sage and/or QuickBooks
- Strong bookkeeping and reconciliation skills
- The ability to work independently without close supervision
- Good Excel, Word and general IT skills

Candidates whose bookkeeping experience has been solely within industry or an internal finance department will not be suitable for this particular position.

You don't need to be ACA or ACCA qualified. What matters is that you're a strong, experienced practice bookkeeper who understands client work and can be trusted to take responsibility for it.

Why consider it?

The firm has built a particularly strong reputation for looking after its people. Staff retention is excellent, there is a supportive and collegiate working environment, and people are given autonomy while still having an experienced team around them when they need it.

You'll be joining:
- A highly regarded, long-established accountancy practice
- A firm with an established and varied client base
- A business entering a significant period of investment and growth
- A supportive team with very good staff retention
- Modern, professional offices in central High Wycombe
- A firm with genuine long-term ambitions to grow into the UK Top 100
- An environment where client relationships and quality of service still matter
- A flexi-time system, allowing some flexibility around start and finish times

Salary

£35,000 - £40,000, depending on experience.

If you're already working as a bookkeeper in practice and would like to join a firm with a strong reputation, good people and plenty of ambition for the future, I'd be very interested in speaking with you.

As an employer, we are committed to ensuring the representation of people from all backgrounds regardless of their gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, race, religion, ethnicity, age, neurodiversity, disability status, or any other aspect which makes them unique. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds to apply and would encourage you to let us know if there are steps, we can take to ensure that your recruitment process enables you to present yourself in a way that makes you comfortable.

title: Temporary Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
We are looking for an experienced Purchase Ledger Clerk to join a fast growth and exciting brand in Central Milton Keynes. This is a temporary position, and we need someone who can start either immediately or on a maximum of two weeks' notice.

The Role Reporting directly to the AP Manager, you will take ownership of the day-to-day accounts payable processes. Your main tasks will include:
- Processing supplier invoices and credit notes
- Reconciling supplier statements to ensure accuracy
- Preparing weekly payment runs
- Resolving supplier queries and building relationships with internal stakeholders
- Keeping vendor master data up to date

The Environment

Our client are an 'ethics first' business, and that approach runs through everything they do. You will be based from their Central Milton Keynes office, which is a collaborative, open-plan space with plenty of natural light. They operate a hybrid working model, so you will spend 3 to 4 days a week onsite and work the rest of your week from home with a total of 37.5 hours per week.

What You Bring
- Proven experience in a purchase ledger/accounts payable role
- Quick learner with the ability to get up to speed in the shortest time possible
- Immediate availability or a notice period of under two weeks
- A collaborative and team focused mindset
- Strong attention to detail and organisation skills

The Details
- Pay Rate: 15 - 16 per hour
- Location: Central Milton Keynes
- Working Pattern: Hybrid (3-4 days onsite, 1-2 days remote)
- Contract Type: Temporary

If this setup suits you, send over your CV and we will be in touch.
